products.title: Browse the web with an AI agent in fewer steps
products.summary: A browsing task in, the task done in fewer steps.
products.give: A browsing task and the agent-browser CLI.
products.get: The task done in fewer tool calls: forms, logins, dialogs, uploads and paginated data.
products.tested: Trained and scored with Claude Opus 5.5 through the claude CLI and the agent-browser CLI. On 11 unseen tasks (2 runs each) it used 29.4k weighted tokens per task against 34.2k with no skill, with 22 of 22 correct in every condition. Two of three proposed edit sets made things worse and were rejected by the validation gate. One student model and a small task set; the Setup section was added by hand and was not gated.

products.title: Get a spreadsheet formula that works on your columns
products.summary: The result you want and a few rows in, a formula that works.
products.give: Describe the result you want, paste a few real rows and name your app.
products.get: A formula in your real columns, a test table on your sample, and the edge cases.
products.tested: 2 runs on a public CSV (Claude Sonnet). The first run left out the test table, so we made that section mandatory; the second run included it and the numbers matched.

products.title: Rewrite your CV bullets for one job
products.summary: Your resume bullets and a job post in, clearer bullets, nothing invented.
products.give: Paste your resume bullets and a job post.
products.get: Clearer bullets with every missing number marked for you to confirm, and a table of what the job asks that you do not yet show.
products.tested: 1 real-data run on sample bullets and a public job post (Claude Sonnet). We changed placeholder wording after the run so it never implies a result.

products.title: Write a cold email from a prospect's website
products.summary: A prospect's website in, three emails built on what is on their site.
products.give: A prospect's website and a line on what you sell.
products.get: A three-email sequence and two subject lines, each built on something visible on their site, with the page it came from.
products.tested: 1 real-data run on a public software company's website (Claude Sonnet). Output read and checked: every observation traced to a page, no invented claims.

products.title: Edit a draft so it still sounds like you
products.summary: Samples of your writing and a draft in, the draft in your voice.
products.give: Two or three things you wrote and a draft.
products.get: The draft edited to sound like you, a list of what changed, and flags on claims it cannot support.
products.tested: 1 real-data run on public essay samples and a sample draft (Claude Sonnet). The first run overwrote a file in the test folder, so the skill now says never to modify files.

products.title: Handle the weekly jobs in a Shopify store: six workflows
products.summary: Your store address in, six tools built from your own store data.
products.tested: Every skill in the pack was tested on real public Shopify stores or real public merchant cases and scored against a written rubric. Each ships only when every test scores 8/10 or more.
includes: See how AI shopping assistants read your store
Write support replies from your own store policies
Rewrite thin product descriptions without made-up claims
Fix the search problems on your product pages
Answer a chargeback: the right letter for each reason
Plan your Black Friday sale on your own prices

products.title: Chase a late invoice (UK), with the interest worked out
products.summary: An invoice date and amount in, the interest you can claim and reminder emails.
products.give: One unpaid business invoice (amount, invoice date, and the due date if you agreed one).
products.get: What you can claim under UK late-payment law, with the working and official sources, and three reminder emails to send.
products.tested: 3 real tests built on the facts of published UK court judgments. Figures checked by hand against the script and the judgment.

products.title: Run your holiday let listing: six workflows
products.summary: Your listing and reviews in, six tools built from your own facts.
products.tested: Each of the six skills has 4 tests on real public data, scored by hand against a written rubric. On the latest Claude Sonnet run of each test, every score is 8.5 or 9 out of 10. An independent reviewer re-scored 12 tests and ran 10 fresh cases from another city; every defect it listed as required is fixed in this version. No host has used the output on a live listing yet.

products.title: Plan a page around what searchers want
products.summary: A keyword in, the search intent and an outline to write from.
products.give: A target keyword and the three to five pages that rank for it (URLs, or pasted headings).
products.get: It records each page's structure, classifies the search intent from what ranks, builds a coverage table with counts, names the gaps as its own judgement, and drafts an outline, questions to answer and a meta description.
products.tested: 1 real-data run on three public how-to pages (Claude Sonnet). One was blocked and the run handled it honestly.

products.title: Check an invoice before you send or pay it
products.summary: An invoice in, every difference and missing field listed.
products.give: An invoice, yours or one you received.
products.get: A small script (Python 3 standard library, exact decimal arithmetic) recomputes every line, the subtotal, the discount, the tax and the total, and lists every difference. It lists common fields that are missing and flags date, currency and rounding problems. It gives no tax advice.
products.tested: 1 run on a sample invoice we wrote with planted errors (Claude Sonnet).

products.title: Check your reply to an angry customer before you send it
products.summary: A customer message and your draft in, a repaired reply back.
products.give: The customer's message, your draft reply and your policy.
products.get: It lists what the customer raised and whether the draft answers it, tests every promise against your policy, checks the facts, flags blame, defensive phrases and empty apologies with your exact words, checks there is a next step, and returns a repaired draft. Open decisions are marked [DECIDE]. It never adds a refund or timeline you did not give it.
products.tested: 1 run on a complaint, draft and policy we wrote (Claude Sonnet).

products.title: Browse the web with a local Qwen model, fewer wrong turns
products.summary: A browsing task and your local model in, the task done in fewer tries.
products.give: A browsing task and the agent-browser CLI.
products.get: A local model like Qwen3.8-27B stops guessing addresses and selectors, and gets the task done in fewer tries.
products.tested: Trained and scored with Qwen3.8-27B on a local server, driven by the pi coding agent. On the 8 selection tasks (6 runs each) it got 48 of 48 correct at 36.4k tokens per task, against 21 of 24 at 68.7k with no skill and 47 of 48 at 42.3k with the Claude-trained Agent Browse. These are selection-split figures, the split the gate used to pick it. The held-out test is pending. Three of four tuning attempts were rejected by the gate.

products.title: Check a data file before you rely on it
products.summary: A CSV file in, a profile of every column and the odd rows flagged.
products.give: A CSV.
products.get: It runs a small read-only script (Python 3 standard library) and reports rows, columns, each column's type, blanks, distinct values, ranges, duplicates, mixed formats, stray spaces, case variants and outliers, then lists questions to ask the data's owner. Without code execution it profiles a pasted sample and says so.
products.tested: 1 run on a real public CSV (Claude Sonnet) with the script.

products.title: Read a job post for what the job really is
products.summary: A job post in, what is firm, what is wishful and what to ask.
products.give: Paste a job post.
products.get: It says in plain words what the job is, sorts the requirements into firm, wish and unclear with quotes, lists what the post leaves out (pay, location, hours, team), points out phrases worth a question, and gives you six to eight questions for the recruiter. If you add your background, it says where the fit is strong or weak and what to lead with. It never says anything about the employer beyond the post.
products.tested: 1 run on a real public job post (Claude Sonnet).

products.title: Check a cold email for claims you can't back up
products.summary: Your draft in, a verdict and a version without unsupported claims.
products.give: A cold email draft and the text of the prospect's page.
products.get: It tests every claim about the prospect against that text, flags claims about you that need proof, checks the subject line, the single ask and the length, and lists the commercial email basics from the US FTC's CAN-SPAM guide that the draft is missing. You get a verdict, a claims table, quoted issues and a tightened version with unsupported claims removed.
products.tested: 1 run on a draft we wrote with common flaws and text from a real public homepage (Claude Sonnet).

products.title: Find the claims in a draft that need a source
products.summary: Your draft in, claims ranked by risk with safer wording.
products.give: Paste a draft before you publish.
products.get: Get the claims that need a source, ranked by risk, what would settle each, and safer wording for the ones you cannot back up.
products.tested: 1 real-data run on a public launch post (Claude Sonnet). All 17 flagged claims and both internal conflicts were real.

products.title: Write image descriptions (alt text) for your products
products.summary: Your store in, alt text for every product photo as an import file.
products.give: Your store URL, a product URL, or your product export CSV.
products.get: Alt text for every product image, written while looking at the photo. Comes as a Shopify import CSV, a review sheet, and a paste-by-hand list for products with variant images.
products.tested: Tested on 6 real cases from public Shopify stores, including three product export CSVs. Final scores: 10, 10, 9, 10, 9 and 10 out of 10.

products.title: Rewrite your holiday let listing
products.summary: Your listing text in, three titles and a description from your own facts.
products.give: Paste your listing title, description and amenities.
products.get: Three titles under 50 characters, a description within 500 characters and the section fields, built only from your own facts, plus a list of anything to confirm.
products.tested: Tested on 4 real public listings. Final Claude Sonnet scores: 9, 8.5, 9 and 8.5 out of 10.

products.title: Check how AI search tools read your website
products.summary: Your website address in, a score out of 100 and fixes in order.
products.give: A website URL.
products.get: A 0 to 100 score from 8 checks on whether AI search tools can read the site, the evidence for each check, and a fix list in order.
products.tested: Tested on 8 real public websites, as a skill and (four of them) as a pasted prompt, two also on a second model, then re-scored after two independent reviews. The score matched our script in every run. Final scores: 8.5, 8.5, 8.5, 8.5, 9, 9, 9 and 9 out of 10.

products.get: A ready-to-paste PR title and summary, risk notes, a test plan from what is stated, and the questions a reviewer is likely to ask.
products.tested: 1 real-data run on four public commits (Claude Sonnet).

products.tested: Tested on 4 real public Shopify stores with Gorgias, Zendesk, Shopify Inbox and neutral output, scored against a written rubric. Every policy fact in the macros was checked against the stores' own policy text.

products.get: Get a user-facing changelog with the commit behind every line, and the vague commits flagged.

products.title: Reply to reviews without promising what you can't give

products.give: Your reviews (pasted, CSV, or a public review page).
products.get: A reply for each review, matched to its tone. It never promises refunds you didn't approve, and it flags reviews that need you personally.
products.tested: Tested on 3 real public review sets (Judge.me and Trustpilot). Final runs: 9, 9.5 and 9 out of 10.

products.give: A diff and the tests.
products.get: Get each behaviour the change adds marked Covered, Not covered or Unknown, and ranked test cases for the gaps.
